findings.title: `_select_arch()` keys off OS, not GPU availability — Linux without CUDA crashes at startup, contradicting A7
findings.description:
The updated `_select_arch()` returns `qd.cuda` for `platform.system() == "Linux"` unconditionally and only warns/falls back for platforms that are neither Darwin nor Linux. The parent slice plan's (146) entry requires: "`quadrants` uses Metal on macOS and CUDA on Linux; **if neither is detected** it warns and falls back to `qd.cpu`" — detection of GPU availability, not of the OS string. The doc's own Open Notes (line 382) state that `qd.init()` raises when "CUDA driver absent", and `setup()` propagates that exception, so on a Linux host with no CUDA the server exits at startup. A7 ("A host with no Metal and no CUDA starts successfully with `backend: quadrants` … falls back to `qd.cpu`") is therefore unachievable as specified — a Linux laptop or `ubuntu-latest` CI runner is the most likely "no GPU" case.

This interacts badly with the default: because `ComputeConfig.backend` defaults to `quadrants` (lines 51-63), every existing config that omits the block — including `config/default.yaml`, `tests/load/conftest.py`, and the `ServerConfig` fixtures in `tests/test_server.py` / `tests/test_main.py` — now requires a working GPU. Combined with `addopts = "-m 'not load'"` and the CI workflow running `uv run pytest -m load` on `ubuntu-latest` (no GPU), the existing jobs would begin failing rather than skipping. The design specifies no test/config migration and no capability probe.

findings.title: REFLECT's velocity correction is silently dropped on the GPU path
findings.description:
Line 209 states: "For `BoundsPolicy.REFLECT` and `BoundsPolicy.SOFT`: same sync-back pattern." That pattern (line 213) is `notify_positions_modified(...)` → `state.upload_positions(...)` — positions only. But `apply_bounds_policy` for `REFLECT` mutates **both** positions and velocities (`_apply_reflect` in `src/migratory_server/bounds_enforcement.py` writes `positions[x_low_mask, 0]`, `velocities[x_low_mask, 0]`, etc.). On the GPU path the arrays passed in come from `TickResult.from_quadrants_fields` and are host-side copies, so the velocity flip affects only the serialized wire message — the device keeps the outward-pointing velocity and the next tick integrates the agent back out of bounds. The client and the simulation would then disagree about velocities. A4 ("All four `BoundsPolicy` variants produce valid … positions after 100 ticks on the GPU path") fails for `reflect` as specified.

Either the sync-back must carry velocities too (the driver's public interface currently has no such method), or `reflect` should be rejected at startup on the GPU path. Given the doc's own note that reflect/soft "are rare at the N values this slice targets," the lighter option — fail explicitly for non-`wrap`/non-`open` policies on the `quadrants` backend, per the project's "fail explicitly, never silent fallback" rule — would remove `_positions_dirty` complexity that only `wrap` actually needs.

findings.title: Soft bounds and predator-prey interactions are silently ignored on the GPU path
findings.description:
`build_forces()` appends a `WorldBoundsRepulsor` when `world_bounds.policy is BoundsPolicy.SOFT`, and appends `FlightForce`/`PursuitForce` when `simulation.interactions` is non-empty (`src/migratory_server/force_builder.py`). The fused kernel accumulates only cohesion, separation, alignment, leadership, momentum and propulsion (`quadrants_fused_kernels.py::fused_force_integrate_kernel`) — it has no repulsor and no predator/prey terms. Meanwhile `apply_bounds_policy` returns immediately for `SOFT` ("No-op: WorldBoundsRepulsor handles this via forces"), so on the GPU path soft bounds are enforced by *nothing*: agents drift outside `[0, width] × [0, height]`. The doc asserts the opposite at line 209 and in A4, and even plans a pointless per-tick host→device upload for a policy under which `apply_bounds_policy` modifies nothing.

The same silent-divergence applies to configured `interactions`, which the doc never mentions at all. This violates the architecture's "Preserve behavioral fidelity across scaling tiers" goal (140-arch §Design Goals) and the project rule against silent fallbacks. The design needs an explicit supported-configuration gate for `backend: quadrants` (reject `soft` and `interactions` at startup with a clear error, or implement them), stated in §Scope.

findings.title: New-client SNAPSHOT reads `EntityManager.state`, which the GPU path never updates
findings.description:
A3 claims "Downstream code (`client_manager.broadcast`, sim logger) requires zero changes" and §Scope/§Architecture claim the server call site is unchanged. But the connect-time snapshot path is a *separate* consumer of engine state: `make_snapshot_builder(em, world_bounds)` closes over the entity manager and calls `TickResult.from_numpy_state(em.state, em.count)` (`src/migratory_server/clients.py`). On the CPU path this is current because `tick()` mutates those arrays in place. On the GPU path nothing writes back to `em.state`: `setup_from_server()` uploads from it once, downloads go into a fresh `TickResult`, and `notify_positions_modified()` stores the array inside the driver. Every client connecting after the first tick therefore receives a SNAPSHOT of the spawn-time state, while subsequent STATE_UPDATEs carry correct GPU positions — a visible "jump" on connect and a divergence between the two message types.

The design needs to specify one of: write downloaded positions back into `em.state` each tick, or change `make_snapshot_builder` to consume the latest `TickResult` (which re-opens the `TickResult` lifetime rule the slice 140 contract documents). This is a genuine missing integration point, not a restatement, and should be listed in §Files Changed.

findings.title: The production→bench dependency is not eliminated by moving `GpuAgentState`
findings.description:
The Open Note claims the move "eliminates the production→bench import dependency before it is created." It does not. The driver's `step()` must run `build_spatial_hash(state)` and `fused_force_integrate_kernel(...)` (line 122), and those live in `src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_kernels.py`, which is not moved and is explicitly declared unchanged ("The bench backends … are **not changed**", line 301). So `src/migratory_server/gpu_driver.py` imports the bench package regardless. Additionally, the relocated module still carries bench dependencies: `quadrants_fused_state.py` imports `migratory.bench.backends.numpy_backend._build_initial_state` and `migratory.bench.workload.Workload` (for the unchanged `setup(workload)`), so `src/migratory/gpu/agent_state.py` would import `migratory.bench.*` at module scope — a production package depending on the bench harness.

The design should either move the kernel module (and split the workload-dependent initializer) into `migratory/gpu/`, or state plainly that the production GPU path depends on the bench kernels for this slice and record it as accepted debt with the cut-over deferred.

findings.title: Files Changed understates the move's blast radius; A5 is inconsistent with it
findings.description: The Files Changed table lists only `quadrants_fused_backend.py` as updating its import, then states the bench backends are "not changed" and A5 requires "All existing bench tests pass without modification." But `src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_kernels.py` imports `GpuAgentState` from `quadrants_fused_state`, and `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused.py` and `tests/bench/test_quadrants_fused_kernels.py` import `from migratory.bench.backends.quadrants_fused_state import GpuAgentState` directly. Moving the module without a re-export shim means at least three more files change or those tests fail to import — so either A5's "without modification" is false, or a compatibility shim (a thinner, cheaper option for this slice) must be specified.

findings.title: `sync_from_entity_manager()` is under-specified for a count change
findings.description: `sync_from_entity_manager()` is documented only as "Re-upload CPU state after spawn/despawn," and `setup_from_server()` derives `n` from `entity_manager.count` — the per-agent fields and `sorted_agent_ids` are sized to that `N`. A count change is therefore not a data re-upload: it requires field reallocation (and Quadrants recompiles kernels on shape change, as the slice 145 design already documents), plus re-binding of the module-global field aliases that `_bind_state_fields` maintains. The doc also only justifies "`qd.init()` called once at server startup" (line 32); it says nothing about the cost or recurrence of reallocation. Separately, nothing in the live server changes the count after startup (grep shows `spawn_population` only, at `server.py` startup; `spawn_entity`/`remove_entity` have no production call sites), so this machinery is currently unexercised even though plan (146) assigns the behavior — specify the resize semantics and note the slice ships it unexercised by the live loop, or defer it with the plan's intent recorded.

findings.title: Driver tests cannot run as specified: "CPU-only" vs a GPU-only setup, in a shared pytest process
findings.description: Line 307 says "All tests are CPU-only (skip if `quadrants` not importable or if GPU not available)," while test 5 is "GpuSimulationDriver.setup + step (GPU-required, skip if unavailable)" and the driver has no CPU arch on Darwin/Linux by construction (see the first finding). Worse, Open Note line 382 states that a second `qd.init()` in the same process is undefined behavior and that tests exercising `setup()` "must either use `finalize()` + process isolation or be marked to run in a subprocess" — yet `tests/server/test_gpu_driver.py` places tests 5–8 in the ordinary in-process suite that `pytest tests/ -q` runs alongside everything else. As written, the slice's core paths are skipped everywhere except a GPU dev box, and on a GPU host they risk the UB the note itself warns about. Specify the isolation mechanism (subprocess-marked, or a single process-scoped setup/teardown fixture) and correct the "CPU-only" claim.

findings.title: Config error type contradicts the existing validation convention and the walkthrough's expected output
findings.description: Tests 3 and 4 specify `ValueError` for an invalid backend and an out-of-range `subdivision_factor`, and the error walkthrough (line 356) expects the server to "exit with a clear `ValueError` naming the invalid value." The established convention in `src/migratory_server/config.py` is `ConfigError` with a full field path (e.g. the analogous `simulation.spatial.backend` validation), and `__main__.py` catches only `ConfigError`, printing "Configuration error: …" and exiting 1. As written, the specified tests would fail and the walkthrough would observe a different message than documented. State `ConfigError` and the expected `simulation.compute.backend` field path.
